guarantee verb

promise that something will be so; answer for

also vouch for, answer for, I guarantee, can you guarantee, stand surety, be responsible for

classical

Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.3: praestābō sūmptum nusquam melius posse pōnī
Cic. Fam. 1.4.3: Ego tibi ā vī … praestāre nihil possum

praestō, praestāre, praestitī, praestitum

verb, first conjugation

guarantee, answer for, vouch for

To make oneself answerable for something (Lewis & Short): with an object, damnum praestāre, to make good a loss; with an accusative and infinitive, to guarantee that something is or will be so. Its commoner senses are to excel (praestat, it is better) and to supply or show (officium praestāre, to do one’s duty).

Other words

  • spondeō, spondēre, spopondī, spōnsum — pledge, vouch for (formally)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 4.2.118 (old numbering): Spondēn’ tū istud? — Spondeō. (Lewis & Short)

    The solemn pledge of a Roman contract (see promise); to stand surety for someone, prō aliquō spondēre (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • praestābō sūmptum nusquam melius posse pōnī

    I guarantee the money could not be better spent anywhereCic. Q. fr. 3.1.3

  • Ego tibi ā vī, hāc praesertim imbēcillitāte magistrātuum, praestāre nihil possum

    Against violence, especially with the magistrates as weak as they are, I can guarantee you nothingCic. Fam. 1.4.3

  • quis potest praestāre semper sapientem beātum fore, cum vel in omnibus hīs ūnō tempore esse possit?

    who can guarantee that the wise man will always be happy, when he may meet all these at one and the same time?Cic. Tusc. 5.29

See also promise, word, guarantee, sure.
